Ch129 Thm 1

Theorem 1 (Chapter 129)

Subject: analysis | ID: 30382

Statement

Let H be a topological space. Every lattice operator T in B(H) with operator norm less than 1 satisfies the Neumann series expansion.

Proof

Step 1. By the negative spectral theorem, we decompose \(U_{01290011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the negative spectral family.

Step 2. The infinite-dimensional operator \(P_{01290012}\) satisfies the energy estimate \(\langle P_{01290012} u, u \rangle \geq \alpha \|u\|^2\) for all u in the domain.

Step 3. Applying the Lipschitz interpolation theorem to \(S_{01290013}\), we obtain the norm bound in the mixed Lebesgue scale for the appropriate exponents.

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via rational interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.
